open_questions.detail: The small category label under each item name (Classic, Specialty, Vegetarian, Sides & Drinks) is rendered in accent-green (#2A7043) for the two sampled nodes (13:49 'Classic', 13:65 'Specialty'). Fill color for the 'Vegetarian' and 'Sides & Drinks' labels was not independently re-sampled per-node in this pass, and the PNG does not show an obviously different hue for them at this resolution — it is unclear whether ALL four categories share one green, or each category gets its own color token.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume a single shared accent-green (#2A7043) category-label color for all four categories, since only one distinct color token exists in the frame's token palette for this role.

options.label: One shared accent-green (#2A7043) for all categories — the only green token present in the frame
A distinct color per category (would require sampling each of the 9 card labels individually against the render, and likely adding new color tokens beyond the 7 already distilled)

open_questions.topic: 'Add to Cart' vs. 'Add to Order' button copy
open_questions.detail: Every card's button reads 'Add to Cart' in this Figma frame, but the existing PizzaCard.tsx component hardcodes the label 'Add to Order'.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume this frame supersedes the landing-page copy and PizzaCard's label prop should be updated to 'Add to Cart' for the menu page (and likely globally, for consistency).

options.label: Rename PizzaCard's button label to 'Add to Cart' everywhere, including the FeaturedPizzas section on the landing page
Keep 'Add to Order' on the landing page's FeaturedPizzas cards but use 'Add to Cart' only on the menu-browse grid (would require a label prop)

open_questions.topic: PizzaCard / PizzaData used for non-pizza items
open_questions.detail: The grid includes a focaccia and a tiramisu dessert rendered with the identical PizzaCard shape, but the existing type is named PizzaData with fields (id, name, price, description, image) and no category field.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume PizzaData is generalized in place (rename to MenuItemData, add a required category field) rather than introducing a parallel non-pizza card type, since the visual design uses one card shape for every item.

open_questions.detail: Node 13:187 sits at absolute (980, 2216) inside the footer's vertical range (footer runs 1956-2432), suggesting it is a fixed/floating overlay pinned to the bottom-right of the viewport rather than a document-flow element that scrolls into the footer. The static frame capture cannot show scroll behavior.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume position: fixed, bottom-right of the viewport, visible once at least one item is added to the cart, so it does not visually collide with the in-flow footer content during normal scrolling.

options.label: position: fixed bottom-right overlay, independent of scroll/footer
Static element placed at the end of the menu grid, in document flow just before the footer

open_questions.detail: The sticky cart summary (13:190) uses a distinct 'shopping-bag' vector glyph, but the codebase's IconName union (src/components/common/Icon.tsx) only defines 'shopping-cart', not 'shopping-bag'.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume a new 'shopping-bag' IconName/path is added to Icon.tsx rather than reusing 'shopping-cart' for both header and sticky-summary, since the frame renders two visually distinct glyphs.

open_questions.topic: No empty-state design for a category with zero matches
open_questions.detail: The filter row implies client-side filtering (All / Classic / Specialty / Vegetarian / Sides & Drinks) but the frame only shows the 'All' state with 9 populated cards; no empty-state or loading-state is drawn for a filter that (hypothetically) matches nothing.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume every category always has at least one matching item (as seen in this 9-item set) and defer designing an empty state until product content proves otherwise.
